lesson_snippet.title: Introduction to RAG

sections.heading: What RAG Means
sections.content: RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It retrieves relevant documents from a knowledge base and provides them as context to an LLM. The LLM then generates a response grounded in this retrieved information. RAG does not retrain or modify the LLM in any way.

lesson_snippet.summary: RAG enhances LLMs by providing external knowledge through retrieval.

name: RAG retraining hallucination
description: Contains the claim that RAG retrains the LLM

lesson_snippet.title: Introduction to RAG

sections.heading: How RAG Works
sections.content: RAG retrains the LLM whenever new documents are added to the knowledge base. This ensures the model always has the latest information built into its parameters.

lesson_snippet.summary: RAG retrains models with new data.

sections.heading: How RAG Works
sections.content: The system uses dense embeddings with HNSW indexing and cosine similarity to perform approximate nearest neighbor search in a high-dimensional vector space.

lesson_snippet.title: An Examination of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Methodologies

sections.heading: Theoretical Framework
sections.content: The paradigmatic shift in natural language processing necessitates a comprehensive understanding of the epistemological foundations underlying retrieval-augmented generation architectures, wherein the concatenation of retrieved textual artifacts with the contextual window of transformer-based language models facilitates the amelioration of hallucination phenomena.

lesson_snippet.summary: This examination elucidates the theoretical underpinnings of RAG.
